topic: twitch streamers can opt out of AI training
headline_marked: Twitch [[defaults to AI training]] on your streams; opt-out available
headline: Twitch defaults to AI training on your streams; opt-out available
summary: The Amazon-owned platform is automatically opting all users into its generative AI training feature, sparking backlash from creators.
details: Twitch has confirmed it will use streamers' content to train its generative AI models, with all users automatically opted in by default. This move has generated significant backlash from the creator community, with thousands demanding an opt-in setting instead.

Users can opt out of this feature through their account settings on the web or mobile app. The setting can be found under Settings > Security and Privacy > Training for Generative AI. Opting out in one place applies to all.

Disabling this setting specifically prevents your content from being used for generative AI model training. Twitch clarifies that it may still use user data for other AI features like AutoMod and captions, but this data is not retained for GenAI training.

Twitch's Chief Product Officer Mike Minton stated that the opt-out setting will not impact a streamer's reach or discoverability on the platform. He also explained that the default opt-in was chosen because 'if it was opt in, nobody would opt in.'

Minton acknowledged the community's frustration, calling it 'not a fan favorite' and 'very upsetting.' He noted that many other platforms, including YouTube (Google) and Meta (Facebook/Instagram), also use user content for AI training, often without an opt-out option.

He also suggested that other AI labs may be scraping Twitch content regardless of permission, stating it's a 'reasonable assumption that almost any publicly available content is being used for model training in one form or another, whether permitted or not.'
